scope: Restricted top-level getter/setter body updates on host ARM64 with AOT callers and bytecode helpers
observations: Getter and setter bodies install independently while unchanged AOT callers, generated wrappers and global storage remain in the baseline.

Same-named accessors in different libraries, a getter and setter split across a part, private access, compound assignment and a getter-returned callback match independently compiled original-source AOT.
Old AOT retains bytecode-created closures across observed young-generation GC and an await; generic function results match original-source AOT.
Annotated and external top-level accessors are rejected by this restricted compiler.
not_accepted: Full M1 language/runtime compatibility and the historical native suite were not rerun.
Flutter cold-start activation, Android/iOS physical-device execution, signing, rollback and performance gates remain unverified.
Package accessors, annotation preservation, broader language-version combinations and accessor signature/layout changes need separate validation.
